adversarial-red-team.name: financingDilution
adversarial-red-team.basis: ATM issuance and the July equity offering increased share count to fund operations/growth.

adversarial-red-team.name: integrationRisk
adversarial-red-team.basis: Stereolabs adds useful vision/software capability but requires integration across products, teams and go-to-market.

adversarial-red-team.name: profitabilityConversion
adversarial-red-team.basis: Q2 gross margin improved while GAAP net loss and adjusted EBITDA loss remained negative.

expectations-execution.name: product growth
expectations-execution.basis: 55% year-over-year product revenue growth and higher unit shipments show operating demand expansion.

expectations-execution.name: profitability conversion
expectations-execution.basis: Gross margin improved year over year while adjusted EBITDA remained negative.

thesisQuality.basis: Q2 revenue grew 56% YoY, product revenue 51%, shipments exceeded 17,000 and the Stereolabs combination broadens lidar into cameras, compute and perception software; durable moat remains unproven.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Q2 revenue was $54.6M, GAAP gross margin 49% and adjusted EBITDA loss improved to $4M; cash and short-term investments were substantial, but GAAP and adjusted losses persist.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: Sep 25 market cap was about $3.15B versus roughly $205M trailing revenue and negative earnings, producing a demanding sales multiple despite strong growth and cash resources.

catalystScore.basis: Q3 revenue guidance of $54.5M-$57.5M, Rev8 adoption and Stereolabs product integration provide identifiable operating catalysts; timing of profitability conversion remains uncertain.

governancePower.basis: Management has delivered repeated product growth and improving margins, but repeated equity financing and acquisition integration limit evidence for a stronger capital-allocation band.

alignment2036.basis: Lidar, stereo vision, AI compute and perception software address durable physical-AI needs across robotics, industrial automation, automotive and smart infrastructure.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: The same sensing/perception stack serves industrial, robotics, automotive and smart-infrastructure markets and can reuse software, compute and sensor-fusion capabilities across them.

bottleneckControl.basis: Reliable machine perception is important to autonomy, but competing lidar, camera, radar and integrated OEM stacks prevent evidence of scarce system-level control.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Demand spans multiple physical-AI verticals and two major sensing modalities, reducing dependence on one application while retaining exposure to automation capital cycles.

substitutionResilience.basis: Multi-modal lidar-plus-vision and perception software improve adaptability, but alternative sensors and suppliers remain credible substitutes by use case.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Current filings support ongoing high-volume shipments, but the reviewed evidence does not establish tested multi-source redundancy for critical sensing/compute inputs; unknowns cap the score near mixed.

pricingPower.basis: Gross margin improved to 49% as volume and operating efficiency rose, but evidence does not isolate price realization from mix, volume or cost efficiency and competitive sensor markets constrain confidence.

riskEvidence.basis: Persistent losses, substantial 2026 equity issuance/dilution, acquisition integration and credible sensor substitution create above-moderate risk despite strong growth and liquidity.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Recent SEC and issuer operating evidence is detailed and identity/tradability are validated; independent Sep 25 valuation is available, while governance, supplier redundancy and post-acquisition unit economics remain incompletely isolated.

scoreRecord.thesis: Ouster is building a broader physical-AI perception platform with strong product growth and improving gross margins, but valuation, dilution and incomplete profitability keep the underwriting balanced rather than exceptional.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: Growth fails to convert to durable positive cash generation before competition, substitution or repeated equity issuance erodes per-share value.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Q3 2026 results and guidance, especially revenue growth, gross-margin durability, adjusted EBITDA conversion and evidence of Stereolabs cross-sell.

items.risk: Acquisition integration and multi-sensor platform complexity can raise execution costs and dilute focus.
Prior-quarter royalty revenue was largely one-time, so headline sequential revenue comparisons can misstate underlying product trajectory.
Successor bottleneck shifts from sensor availability to integration cost, perception software quality, compute efficiency and OEM qualification.
Repeated equity financing can dilute per-share upside if operating cash generation does not catch up with growth investment.
Sensor-market competition and modality substitution can pressure pricing even as physical-AI adoption grows.
